samples.summary: Split-propagation of headingLevel onto new list-items contradicts the change's own stated Non-goal
samples.evidence: The branch's plan doc `docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md:50-51` lists as a Non-goal: "Splitting a bulleted heading (Enter) — the new item stays a plain list item, as today." The diff does the opposite in three places: `applySplitBlock` now keeps `headingLevel` when `newBlockType === 'list-item'` (block-helpers.ts:256-262), and `yorkie-doc-store.ts:2049-2056` and `:2141-2147` copy `headingLevel` onto split-off list-items. The design doc (docs/design/docs/docs.md:172-176) was updated to describe the new behavior, so the doc set now contradicts the plan's Non-goals rather than the Non-goal being retracted. Either the plan's Non-goal must be revised as part of this change, or the split propagation belongs in a follow-up.

samples.summary: `unlistedBlockType` restores headings only; bulleted Title/Subtitle still flatten to paragraph
samples.evidence: `unlistedBlockType` keys purely off `block.headingLevel`, and `MemDocStore.setBlockType` only preserves `headingLevel`. A `title` or `subtitle` block that is bulleted therefore loses its type permanently and un-bulleting yields a paragraph — the same destroyed-on-a-reversible-action complaint the issue raises for headings, in the same toolbar dropdown (`STYLE_OPTIONS` includes title/subtitle). The design doc does not record this asymmetry as intentional.

samples.summary: HTML clipboard round trip drops the remembered heading level of a bulleted heading
samples.evidence: `resolveBlockMeta` maps `<li>` to `{ type: 'list-item', listKind }` with no `headingLevel`, and HTML serialization of a list-item emits `<li>` without the level. So copy/paste of a bulleted heading through the HTML flavor produces a bullet with no memory, and un-listing it gives body text — the very failure mode the change fixes elsewhere. Not mentioned in the design-doc note that claims the level "round-trips ... like any other block attribute".

samples.summary: Design-doc claim that every reader gates on `type === 'heading'` is slightly overstated
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2793` (and `text-box-editor.ts:1098`) return `headingLevel` from `getBlockType()` ungated by type; the gating happens one layer up in the toolbar helpers (`getBlockLabel`, `blockTypeToStyleId`). The invariant the doc asserts is enforced by consumers, not by the API surface, which makes the retained-level representation easy to break for a future caller of `getBlockType()`.

verdict.reason: All four claimed locations check out verbatim. The plan doc still lists "Splitting a bulleted heading (Enter) — the new item stays a plain list item, as today." as a Non-goal (todo.md:50-51), and its Steps list (34-44) contains no split work. Yet block-helpers.ts:260-262 explicitly retains headingLevel when newBlockType === 'list-item' (with a comment saying the split hands the heading memory to the new bullet), and yorkie-doc-store.ts:2051-2056 and 2144-2147 mirror that onto the Yorkie tree attrs. Meanwhile docs/design/docs/docs.md:172-176 documents the split propagation as intended behavior. So the change implements and canonically documents behavior its own plan declares out of scope, and nothing in the lessons file or the design doc's Non-Goals section (docs.md:39-49) retracts the Non-goal. This is unreconciled scope creep / design-doc discipline, which is in the design-fit lane and rated major by the rubric ("exceeds a stated Non-Goal"). No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, no guard makes it unreachable, and it is not out of lane.
